chapter: Heroes, heard bands and Lunceford's life on the road
title: Why he admired Sid Catlett's hands, and the match grip
summary: Crawford praises Catlett's natural hands and says modern drummers are noisemakers who hold sticks like clubs; Billy Kyle's drinking comes up.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: What made him great to you?
His hands and his thinking. He'd fit in anybody's band. Mostly played in combos, with Louie Armstrong, people like that.

Our dear friend, Kyle, who was married to Billie Kyle, the great pianist, she told me about a lot of incidents that happened, you know. You know, this is her experience. She's been around. And Billie, he died from alcohol. Oh, that guy used to drink as much as a quart a day. George, ch yes, he was a heavy drinker.
Well, are we running out? I want to stop and let you do some talking.
Well, I wanted you to talk more about Catlett. When you say his -- what you liked about him was his hands, you --

Oh, the man was a natural drummer. I'm telling you, he was just a natural drummer. His hands, he played with his left hand this way, you know. Up here was something else. Now, how in the world he played that, well, that's just the way he played. (inaudible)
Yeah, that way, right flat over the snare drum.
Well, like what they call a match grip today?
I guess so. I don't know what a match grip is.
Well (inaudible) match grip is like that with both hands.

Oh, well, these young guys nowadays, man, they ain't no drummers. They're just noisemakers. But I look at them play now, and they hold the butt of the stick and play with that on the drums and tom-toms, cymbals. diddy-ding-diddy-ding, they play dang-dang-dang, you know, all that with a backbeat over here and holding the sticks like clubs. You know, like a club, not like you would hold them or --
-- out of New York but in New York. He was playing with somebody, because he to me was one of the great drummers of that time, and I wish I could do some of the things that he did on the drums.
